title: Shared value definitions of the Arma Reforger backend API
$comment: Hand-written from what the captures in out/mitm-capture*.jsonl showed on Arma Reforger 1.8.0.13, plus the field names the server binary and the generated script classes carry. There is no root type here: every definition is referenced by an endpoint schema in this directory. A value that was only ever seen with one example is typed loosely (a string, with the observed example in the description); a value the game treats as a closed set is an enum. The patterns are part of the specification - scenarioId is the {16 hex}Missions/Name.conf form this repository insists on, modId is 16 hex characters without braces, and a token is a three-part JWS.

uuid.description: A lowercase hyphenated UUID. Used for the server's own ids (serverId, providerServerId, dedicatedServerId, roomId, dedicatedHostId) and for a player's Game Identity (identityId, userId).

identityId.description: A player's Game Identity id, as the backend calls it: the identityId in the server log, the userId of a ban, and the ownerId of the game client's own owner token are the same value. See docs/en/ArmaReforger_Profile_EN.md section 5.6.

token.description: A three-part JWS, the form ownerToken.bin takes: header.payload.signature, RS512. The server sends the owner token back as accessToken on every lobby S2S call. 50 characters for the header and payload plus a 342-character signature in the captured files; a pattern rather than a length, because the payload grows with the claims.

accessToken.description: A server access token, from servers/auth. A three-part JWS like the owner token, but signed RS256 with a `kid` in its header, and its payload is {iat, exp, id, aid, t} - id is the serverId, aid an account id, t the serverType and exp = iat + the expireIn of the answer. It is a *server-typed* token: userProfiles/getMetadata refuses it with `Unsupported accessToken type`, the same refusal the owner tokens get.

sessionTicket.description: An opaque ticket the backend issues for one player's join and the server presents in rooms/acceptPlayer. 512 characters in the one captured request; not a JWS.

secret.description: An opaque per-session secret returned with the accepted player (144 characters in the capture). Its purpose was not established.

clientVersion.description: The game's short version, three numbers. Observed: 1.8.0.

gameVersion.description: The game's full version, four numbers. Observed: 1.8.0.13, which is the build these captures were made on.

scenarioId.description: The scenario resource id: the 16-hex-character GUID in braces followed by the resource path. Observed: {ECC61978EDCC2B5A}Missions/23_Campaign.conf. The server sends it in both registration bodies, so a wrong GUID is rejected by the backend as well as by the game - see docs/en/ArmaReforger_ServerConfig_EN.md section 4.

modId.description: A Workshop addon's GUID: exactly 16 uppercase hex characters, no braces, no dashes. Observed: 6653028F468BD115.

name.description: Display name the server sends along; observed: GTG_Licences.

platformId.description: Which platform build is talking. Observed on this machine: ReforgerSteam. Other values exist (the binary carries ReforgerXbox/ReforgerPSN-style names) but were not observed.

supportedGameClientType.description: A client platform the server accepts. The enum is taken from the PLATFORM_PC / PLATFORM_XBL / PLATFORM_PSN strings in ArmaReforgerServer.exe 1.8.0.13; PLATFORM_PC is the only one observed in a request.

hostAddress.description: ip:port as handed to clients - the address the server registers, identical to the hostAddress clients receive back in the room. Observed: 127.0.0.1:2005. See docs/en/ArmaReforger_ServerConfig_EN.md section 5.1 on publicAddress.

posixSeconds.description: A Unix timestamp in seconds. Used for ban createdAt/expiresAt and for the room's updated/detailsUpdatedAt.

isoTimestamp.description: An ISO-8601 timestamp with a zone. Observed in the game config's createdAt and the Workshop's createdAt/updatedAt (the latter as 2025-09-09T16:18:13.000000Z).

limit.description: 25 in the captured request, which is also the page size RCON shows for #ban list.

status.description: The backend's acknowledgement. Every simple lobby S2S answer in the captures is exactly this object.

apiError.description: How the game API refuses a request. Observed four times while probing userProfiles/getMetadata: HTTP 400 with apiCode InvalidInput, and HTTP 404 with apiCode NotFound for a GET on a POST-only path. Not an enum on apiCode - the values are the API's own and only two were seen.

code.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body: 400 or 404 in the captures.

apiCode.description: The API's own short code. Observed: InvalidInput, NotFound.

message.description: Readable text, and for a validation failure it names the offending fields - `Field 'userIds' must not be empty, found: null.` That is how the request shape of an otherwise undocumented endpoint was established.

uid.description: A per-request id, presumably for support; it changes on every attempt.

accessToken.description: The owner token, sent back on every call after registration.

caller.description: The three fields every lobby S2S request carries. The schemas in this directory repeat them rather than composing with allOf, because additionalProperties:false in a sibling subschema would reject the endpoint's own fields - the same reason schemas/rcon-result.schema.json gives for its shape.

dedicatedServerId.description: The server's own id, from dsConfig.dedicatedServerId of the registration answer.

roomId.description: The room id, which equals providerServerId and the serverId claim inside the owner token.

roomCaller.description: The five fields every room-scoped lobby S2S request carries, repeated by each endpoint for the reason given on caller.

oneOf.description: A stat reported as an aggregate of the frames since the last heartbeat. frameTime is the only member observed in this form.
A stat reported as one number. memory, memory2 and ai_chars_active were observed in this form.
